html:
"Peshemegs" is the map's misspelled label, for 1000, for the Pechenegs, the Turkic nomads who then held the steppe from the lower Danube to the Volga.

Around 1000 they were at the height of their power, raiding Kievan Rus' and serving or fighting the Byzantines. Prince Vladimir built lines of forts south of Kyiv against them. In 1036 Yaroslav the Wise beat them badly outside Kyiv. Pressed from the east by the Cumans, many crossed the Danube into Byzantine lands. In 1091 a Byzantine and Cuman army destroyed most of them at the Battle of Levounion, and the survivors were absorbed by Hungary, Byzantium and their neighbours.
sum: "Peshemegs" is the map's misspelled label, for 1000, for the Pechenegs, the Turkic nomads who then held the steppe from the lower Danube to the Volga.
